title: Identifying endoplasmic reticulum stress-related key genes of vascular dementia using bioinformatics and biological experiments.
authors: Zhao, Yilong; Xing, Wen; Jiang, Lingling; Liu, Xiangrong; Qu, Hui; Chen, Weiqi; Wang, Yilong
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过生物信息学与机器学习筛选血管性痴呆的内质网应激相关关键基因，虽涉及转录因子预测但无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is the second most common type of dementia, yet its pathogenesis is not fully understood, and effective diagnostic and therapeutic tools are lacking. While endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) is associated with VaD and is recognised as a promising target, the exact mechanism remains unclear. This study analysed differentially expressed ERS-related genes in VaD to identify potential diagnostic markers and provide a new perspective for further in-depth research on the role of ERS in VaD. VaD gene expression data (GSE186798) from human patients were obtained from the GEO database for analysis. After intersecting the obtained genes with those in the GeneCards and Molecular Signatures Databases (MSigDB), key ERS-related genes for the diagnosis of VaD were identified as hub genes using bioinformatics and machine learning techniques. Two hub genes, Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor Gamma Coactivator 1-Alpha (PPARGC1A) and SEC61 Translocon Subunit Gamma (SEC61G), exhibited good diagnostic ability for VaD and were validated in the GSE122063 dataset using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. GeneMANIA analysis indicated a robust association between VaD pathophysiology and ERS responses. Hub genes regulated by microRNAs, transcription factors, and chemicals were computationally predicted, and immune cells with varying dysregulation were also observed. In an in vivo bilateral common carotid artery stenosis (BCAS) mouse model, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and Western blotting analyses confirmed the significant downregulation of the hub genes' expression levels. These hub genes may serve as potential diagnostic biomarkers for VaD.
abstract_zh: 血管性痴呆（VaD）是第二种最常见的痴呆类型，然而其发病机制尚未完全阐明，且缺乏有效的诊断和治疗工具。尽管内质网应激（ERS）与VaD相关，并被认为是一个有前景的靶点，但确切机制仍不清楚。本研究分析了VaD中差异表达的内质网应激相关基因，以识别潜在的诊断标志物，并为进一步深入研究ERS在VaD中的作用提供新视角。从GEO数据库获取了人类患者的VaD基因表达数据（GSE186798）进行分析。将获得的基因与GeneCards和分子特征数据库（MSigDB）中的基因取交集后，利用生物信息学和机器学习技术，将用于VaD诊断的关键ERS相关基因鉴定为核心基因。两个核心基因，过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体γ共激活因子1-α（PPARGC1A）和SEC61转位子亚基γ（SEC61G），对VaD表现出良好的诊断能力，并在GSE122063数据集中通过受试者工作特征（ROC）曲线分析进行了验证。GeneMANIA分析表明，VaD病理生理学与ERS反应之间存在稳健关联。通过计算预测了受microRNA、转录因子和化学物质调控的核心基因，并观察到不同失调程度的免疫细胞。在体内双侧颈总动脉狭窄（BCAS）小鼠模型中，定量实时PCR（qRT-PCR）和Western blotting分析证实了核心基因表达水平的显著下调。这些核心基因可能作为VaD的潜在诊断生物标志物。
